answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable bond before it may place orders, with one bond supporting only one active identity. A sable account might trade in an ivory market using a ferrous-backed bond, but creating a thousand accounts still requires a thousand locked bonds. The protocol can slash a bond when an account is proven to double-spend or violate a signed commitment, while honest agents recover it on exit. Sybils are not impossible; they become capital-intensive and expose the attacker to forfeiture.
